 Motor racing-Russell searching for F1 answers after off day in Austin
 By Alan Baldwin 
 Monday, 26 Oct 2026
 | 9:16 AM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 Formula One F1 - United States Grand Prix - Circuit of the Americas, Austin, Texas, U.S. - October 25, 2026 Mercedes' George Russell arrives ahead of the race REUTERS/Kaylee Greenlee 
 AUSTIN, Texas, Oct ⁠25 (Reuters) - George Russell was searching for answers after finishing eighth in a US ⁠Grand Prix won by Formula One champion-in-waiting Mercedes teammateKimi Antonelli on Sunday.
 The Briton ‌started in sixth place on the grid at Austin's Circuit of the Americas, collected a five-second penalty for an incident with McLaren's OscarPiastriand said he had no explanation for his lack of pace other than "just ​not being quick enough."
 “I need to try and understand why ⁠it is. It’s strange when you’re ⁠so far off, so hopefully there’s some answers somewhere. But, anyway, I don’t have ⁠one,” ‌he told Sky Sports television.
 The result left Antonelli on the brink of a coronation, the title surely his for the taking in Mexico next weekend with Russell ⁠still his closest rival but now 123 points behind ​and with a maximum 125 ‌to be won.
 “The pace wasn't good on the first stint," Russell told reporters. “But ⁠when I came ​out of the pits on the hard (tyres), I probably did six laps where I was lapping the same pace asKimi. But then I caught up with Oscar and I just couldn't overtake.
 "Six ⁠good laps, 50 bad laps. I want to understand ​why the pace was so bad on the first stint."
 Team boss Toto Wolff said Russell had just struggled.
 "George for all of us in the team is a champion and has won ⁠in every category and I think he merits to be put in the group of the very best ones. And we've seen that last year," said the Austrian.
 "This year ... we see this variability in results. When we land the car in a way that ​suits him, he's absolutely fast. But when it drops out ⁠of that operational window, he struggles. And he struggles more than maybe Kimi.
 "We just have ​to work it out with him, how there can ‌be such a difference in driving, in performance. ​Because George is not half a second slower, three tenths slower than Kimi. That's just absolutely not the case."
 (Reporting by Alan Baldwin; Editing by Muralikumar Anantharaman)
